r: しょしんわするべからず
mean: never lose the fresh resolve you had as a beginner
lit: you must not forget the beginner's mind

story.text: The Noh master Zeami wrote these words in his treatise on acting, Kakyō (1424). He meant that a performer should never forget how unskilled he was at the start, and should keep in mind the beginner's stage of every period of his career, even in old age. Today it is mostly used to mean keeping the enthusiasm and resolve one had at the start.

use.how: Quoted as a full sentence or with の気持ち, as a motto or reminder, often to newcomers or to people grown used to their work or success: 初心忘るべからずですね。
